definitions.explanation: Words or actions used when meeting someone or on particular occasions.
A formal speech or remarks, especially at ceremonies.

examples.japanese: {挨拶|あいさつ}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なしに→無し：03779_nashi⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: They left without even saying goodbye.

examples.english: There was a speech by the president.

examples.english: The principal gave a long speech at the graduation ceremony.

notes:
{挨拶|あいさつ} covers both everyday greetings and formal speeches or addresses. It is one of the most important social concepts in Japanese culture.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {挨拶|あいさつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to greet
- {挨拶|あいさつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧: to exchange greetings
- ご{挨拶|あいさつ}: greeting (polite form)
- {挨拶|あいさつ}⟦{回|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧: making rounds to greet people (e.g., neighbors, clients)

COMMON GREETINGS:
- ⟦おはようございます→おはよう：05205_ohayou⟧: good morning
- ⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧: hello (daytime)
- ⟦こんばんは→こんばんは：noentry⟧: good evening
- ⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧: goodbye
- ⟦いただきます→いただきます：00946_itadakimasu⟧ / ⟦ごちそうさま→ごちそうさま：00929_gochisousama⟧: meal greetings

CULTURAL NOTE:
Greetings are considered essential in Japan. Children learn {挨拶|あいさつ} early, and failing to greet properly can be seen as rude. In business, {挨拶|あいさつ}⟦{回|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧ (greeting visits) are customary when starting a new position or at the new year.
